newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT- US T-bond futures seen regaining momentum.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT- US T-bond futures seen regaining momentum.

text.p: U.S. Treasury bond futures are regaining upward momentum after a much anticipated correction this week appeared to have ended with only minor losses, technical analysts said.

A bounce in June T-bond futures today above last Friday's 110-10/32 high probably meant a near-term low had been put in on Thursday, and positive bias in various momentum indicators managed to stay intact, they noted.
"Basically, I'm pleased to see the market break through the 110-10/32 area," said Mathew Crosson, director of fixed income at Pegasus Econometrics Group.

"If the market closes above that level, I see a pattern in there -- it's an ascending triangle," he noted. He projected an intermediate-term target for a breakout from that triangle at around 112-8/32.
"The daily and intraday studies remain positive and rising...and I see positive momentum building up on the weekly charts," Crosson added.

David Lockwood, senior interest-rate analyst at Elliott Wave International, agreed that Thursday's low was an important turning point, although recent price action was not providing a clear-cut pattern for Elliott Wave counts.
"From a wave standpoint, there are just so many labels you can put on," Lockwood said. "But all of them say it will be up for several weeks."
He said the 113-area was the closest projection for his wave counts, with various other targets up to 117.

But Lockwood added, "What happens in the next two to three days, I have no idea. Even today, it looks like it should go straight up, but it's kind of like a shark -- if it doesn't keep going straight up it's going to die and we'll wind up with a few days of consolidation."

June T-bonds were up 7/32 at 110-1/32 in mid-morning trade after rising as high as 110-14/32 earlier, boosted by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's comment overnight that he expected economic growth to slow later this year.
The market took the remarks as meaning the Fed might not tighten at the May 20 Federal Open Market Committee meeting or that a rate hike then would be the last of the cycle.
Such a prospect boded particularly well for Eurodollar futures.
"I think the short end is going to benefit the most from any sign the Fed may wait," Crosson said.
He said candlesticks for Euros looked good after overcoming some ominous doji and harami patterns in the last week or so, which had suggested an impending correction.

"I think those patterns were fulfilled when the market touched the lows just yesterday," he said, adding that Thursday's bottoms of 93.55 in December and 93.80 in September would likely hold in the near term.
